survey: A pair of flip-flops seen from above at a slight angle, side by side, toes pointing up and to the right. Each one has a flat coral sole with a raised rim and a field of small dimples in the heel and forefoot. Each has a yellow Y-strap. The toe post rises from the sole between the first and second toe area and splits into two arms. The right arm ends in a slot on the outer edge of the sole near mid-foot. The left arm wraps over the edge on the inner side at about the same place. Both soles lie flat on the background and share one consistent tilt. Neither floats nor cuts through the other. The two sandals are near-identical rather than strictly mirrored left and right. That is a normal simplification, since many cheap flip-flops have symmetric soles, so it is not a construction fault. The strap arms are anchored, the toe post meets the sole, and the soles are believable thickness and shape. A foot could slip in and the sandals would work.
